key_insight: Engineering a non-Markovian bath for a single trapped-ion spin can drive steady states into regimes that a standard Markovian model cannot reach.
engineering_relevance: This shows that structured dissipation can be used as a control knob in quantum reservoir engineering, with a path toward scalable many-body open-system simulators.
method: Trapped-ion quantum simulator of a driven-dissipative spin-1/2 system
Implemented an engineered non-Markovian dissipation channel
Compared steady states against an analogous Markovian bath baseline
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental steady-state comparisons showing that non-Markovian dissipation dramatically alters the qubit steady state relative to Markovian dissipation.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated for a single trapped ion, so extending the engineered bath reliably to larger many-body systems may add control and decoherence challenges.
paper_title: Steady States of a Single Trapped-Ion Spin Coupled to an Engineered Non-Markovian Bath
